identification.summary: Mango Sandstorm (formerly MERCURY; also tracked as MuddyWater) is an Iranian nation-state actor that Microsoft assesses with high confidence is affiliated with Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS) [S1][S2]. Microsoft reports it mainly targets organizations in the Middle East and those doing business with Middle Eastern victims [S1]. In 2022 it exploited Log4j 2 vulnerabilities in internet-facing applications, including SysAid Server instances at Israeli organizations [S1]. In 2023 it enabled a destructive hybrid on-premises and cloud attack carried out by its likely partner Storm-1084 (DEV-1084) under the DarkBit persona [S2][S3].
identification.notes: Microsoft renamed MERCURY to Mango Sandstorm in its April 2023 taxonomy change; Sandstorm is Microsoft's family name for Iranian actors [S1][S2][S4]. Microsoft equates MERCURY with the MuddyWater name used by US Cyber Command [S1] and calls Mango Sandstorm 'a.k.a. MuddyWater' [S3]. Storm-1084 (formerly DEV-1084, DarkBit persona) is a separate Microsoft cluster that Microsoft assesses likely partnered with Mango Sandstorm; its destructive actions should not be merged into Mango Sandstorm's profile [S2]. Other vendor aliases in the base record (Seedworm, Static Kitten, TA450, Boggy Serpens, etc.) were not re-verified in this pass; see gaps.

attribution.sponsor: Iran, Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS) [S1][S2][S3].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft assesses with high confidence that MERCURY/Mango Sandstorm is affiliated with MOIS [S1]. Microsoft reports that US Cyber Command publicly described MuddyWater as 'a subordinate element within the Iranian Ministry of Intelligence and Security' [S1][S2]. Microsoft's 2024 Iran report calls Mango Sandstorm 'MOIS-linked' [S3].
attribution.basis: Microsoft Threat Intelligence telemetry and incident analysis [S1][S2]; Microsoft's citation of the public US Cyber Command attribution of MuddyWater to MOIS [S1][S2]. The Cyber Command primary statement was not opened directly in this research pass.

objectives: Microsoft's reporting shows access operations against Middle Eastern, especially Israeli, organizations [S1]. It also shows Mango Sandstorm providing access that let a partner cluster (Storm-1084) carry out destruction and disruption disguised as criminal ransomware [S2][S3]. That pattern supports both espionage-style access and Iranian state-directed destructive effects against Israel [S2][S3].

sectors: Organizations running vulnerable internet-facing applications (SysAid Server, VMware products affected by Log4j 2) [S1]
Hybrid on-premises and Microsoft cloud (Azure/Microsoft 365) enterprise environments [S2]
regions: Middle East, and organizations doing business with Middle Eastern victims [S1]
targeting.notes: The sources gathered in this pass do not break targeting down by sector; sector data from other vendors and from US government advisories still needs verification (see gaps).

capabilities.summary: Opportunistic exploitation of unpatched internet-facing applications, including Log4j 2 (Log4Shell) in SysAid Server and VMware applications in 2022 [S1]. Follow-on access uses web shells, new local administrator accounts, and startup-folder and registry autostart persistence [S1]. Credential theft uses Mimikatz and SQL-server credential dumping [S1][S2]. Lateral movement uses WMI, RemCom, remote scheduled tasks and encoded PowerShell [S1][S2]. Tunneling and remote access use Ligolo-based tools, Venom proxy, OpenSSH, RPort, and the eHorus remote monitoring product [S1][S2]. The actor also sends spear-phishing from compromised mailboxes with commercial remote-access tools such as ScreenConnect [S1]. In the 2023 hybrid attack, the actors compromised an Azure AD Connect server and used AADInternals to extract connector-account credentials. Microsoft attributes the AADInternals use with high confidence. The actors then abused Global Administrator access, OAuth application permissions and mailbox delegation. Storm-1084 used this access to delete Azure resources and deploy ransomware through Group Policy [S2]. Microsoft notes the actors often waited weeks or months between stages [S2].

campaigns.name: SysAid Server Log4j 2 exploitation against Israeli organizations
campaigns.summary: On 23 and 25 July 2022, MERCURY exploited Log4j 2 in vulnerable SysAid Server instances at Israeli organizations, then used web shells, credential theft and Ligolo/eHorus tunneling. Microsoft assesses the exploitation path with moderate confidence.

campaigns.name: Hybrid destructive attack with Storm-1084 (DarkBit persona)
campaigns.summary: Mango Sandstorm gained access, and Storm-1084 (formerly DEV-1084) then destroyed on-premises and Azure resources under a ransomware cover. Microsoft names the target as an Israeli organization in its 2024 report.

campaigns.name: Microsoft public disclosure of MERCURY / DEV-1084 hybrid attack
campaigns.summary: Microsoft published its analysis linking DEV-1084 to MERCURY through shared infrastructure, tools (RPort, customized Ligolo) and the vatacloud[.]com C2 domain.

diamond.adversary: MOIS-affiliated Iranian operators, per Microsoft's high-confidence assessment and Cyber Command's public attribution of MuddyWater [S1][S3]. Storm-1084 is a likely partner and effects element [S2].
diamond.capability: Log4j 2 exploitation, web shells, Mimikatz, WMI/RemCom lateral movement, Ligolo and Venom tunneling, eHorus/RPort/ScreenConnect remote access, AADInternals, and partner-deployed DarkBit ransomware and cloud resource deletion [S1][S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Multiple actor C2 servers; the vatacloud[.]com C2 domain, attributed to MERCURY with high confidence; Mullvad VPN and a shared IP linking MERCURY and DEV-1084; compromised victim mailboxes used for onward phishing [S1][S2].
diamond.victim: Israeli organizations running SysAid Server [S1]. A hybrid on-premises and Azure organization identified by Microsoft as Israeli [S2][S3]. Middle Eastern organizations and their business partners [S1].
diamond.socioPolitical: Iranian MOIS intelligence and disruptive operations against Israel and the wider Middle East. The criminal-ransomware persona was likely used to mask Iran's involvement [S1][S2][S3].
diamond.technology: Unpatched internet-facing software (Log4j 2), identity synchronization (Azure AD Connect), Global Administrator accounts without MFA, OAuth applications with full_access_as_app, and Group Policy as a mass-deployment channel [S1][S2].

gaps: First-observed date not established from sources fetched in this pass. Base-record references (Unit 42 2017, Kaspersky, Symantec, ClearSky, Talos) could not be reached because of DNS failures.

US government primary documents (US Cyber Command January 2022 statement; CISA/FBI/NSA/NCSC joint advisory on MuddyWater) were not opened; the MOIS attribution here relies on Microsoft's citation of Cyber Command.
MITRE ATT&CK G0069 page could not be fetched in this pass; group description and campaign list not re-verified.

Web search budget was exhausted, so post-2023 activity is not covered. That includes 2024-2026 vendor reporting on newer tooling listed in the base record (MuddyViper, Fooder, RustyWater, Tsundere botnet, LP-Notes) and any activity linked to the 2025 Israel-Iran conflict. Coverage of the actor is therefore incomplete.
Sector-level targeting (government, telecom, oil and gas, defense, etc. as reported by other vendors) not verified in the sources gathered.

Vendor alias mappings beyond MERCURY/MuddyWater (Seedworm, Static Kitten, TA450, Boggy Serpens, COBALT ULSTER, Earth Vetala, TEMP.Zagros) were not re-verified against a fetched Microsoft mapping page.

Boundary between Mango Sandstorm and Storm-1084 remains uncertain: Microsoft does not know whether Storm-1084 is independent, works with other Iranian actors, or is an effects sub-team activated when MERCURY is tasked with destruction [S2].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (OE): Internet-facing enterprise applications (help-desk/ITSM servers such as SysAid, VMware services) and identity synchronization servers (Azure AD Connect) are key cyber terrain. Compromising them gives access to both on-premises and cloud environments [S1][S2]. STEP 2 (effects): Microsoft's reporting shows the actor waiting weeks to months between stages. Access gained for espionage can later be handed to a destructive partner, so dwell time is effectively preparation of the environment [S2]. STEP 3 (adversary template): exploit an N-day in an exposed application, then web shell and local admin account. Next comes credential theft (Mimikatz, SQL dumping), WMI/RemCom lateral movement, and Ligolo/eHorus/RPort tunneling. The actor then pivots to Azure AD Connect and uses AADInternals to escalate to Global Administrator [S1][S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is persistent access and collection against Israeli and Middle Eastern organizations and their partners via unpatched public-facing applications and phishing from compromised mailboxes [S1]. MDCOA is a staged handoff to a destructive partner using a fake ransomware persona. That partner deletes cloud resources and deploys encryption via Group Policy against a partner-nation or US-affiliated hybrid enterprise during a regional crisis [S2][S3]. Candidate indicators: new local administrator accounts on internet-facing servers; RemCom, Ligolo (e.g., vpnui.exe), Venom, eHorus, RPort or unexpected ScreenConnect installs; AADInternals execution on Azure AD Connect hosts; OAuth apps newly granted full_access_as_app; new 'Send on behalf' mailbox delegations; NETLOGON-share payloads distributed via new GPOs [S1][S2].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: correlate on-premises indicators (web shells, tunneling tools) with cloud identity events (Global Admin activity, OAuth consent, Azure resource deletions). Microsoft's 2023 case moved from on-premises to cloud destruction within hours once Global Admin was obtained [S2]. (2) Authorities: the DarkBit-style criminal persona can mislead early characterization. Microsoft assessed the persona as masking Iranian state involvement, so treat ransomware events at Israeli or Middle Eastern partner organizations as potential state-directed activity until assessed otherwise [S2][S3]. (3) Mission assurance: enforce MFA on all privileged and synchronization accounts and prioritize patching of internet-facing Log4j-affected applications. Treat Azure AD Connect servers as tier-0 assets [S1][S2]. (4) Coordination: Mango Sandstorm provides access and a separate cluster carries out effects, so share indicators across both Microsoft clusters and with coalition partners in the region. Detecting the access phase is the main opportunity to prevent the destructive phase [S2].

provenance.importedSummary: The MuddyWater attacks are primarily against Middle Eastern nations. However, we have also observed attacks against surrounding nations and beyond, including targets in India and the USA. MuddyWater attacks are characterized by the use of a slowly evolving PowerShell-based first stage backdoor we call “POWERSTATS”. Despite broad scrutiny and reports on MuddyWater attacks, the activity continues with only incremental changes to the tools and techniques.
